The compose action passes the form-controlled matterId straight into composeMessageFromCustomTemplate/composeMessageFromStandardTemplate, which create a Message (status:'draft') under that matterId after only requireUser. There is no matter existence or access check, so any authenticated user (including clients) can inject draft messages into another tenant's matter thread (create-under-attacker-selected-parent IDOR).

`action` completes an account-recovery/verification flow — issuing a session or writing a new password — without ever comparing the submitted proof against the stored secret. The account is selected by an attacker-supplied identifier alone, so anyone who knows the email address can take the account over. Compare the proof in constant time against the stored (hashed) value and require it to be unexpired and single-use.
